title: The Guardian of Time's Sword
notes: Detective-cast nodes (Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Conan, Inspector Megure) omitted by convention. case_type: murder. The old cases/ file correctly named Teigo Karube as the culprit and had the broad mechanism right, but was very thin: it labeled the weapon a generic 'umbrella' and the location a 'clock tower' -- the transcript clarifies the murder happened in the mansion's grand hall during Rukako's birthday party, the 'clock tower' is the great clock built into the mansion's exterior wall (dial facing the backyard well), and the weapon was Karube's own foldable umbrella fitted with a detachable spike, pulled out of the room and into the well by a fishing-line/weight rig timed off the great clock's hour hand. The old file also omitted the backstory victim (Suou's brother / Karube's childhood friend, the clock technician who drowned in the well four years earlier after Rukako delayed the search for him to keep her party going) and the red-herring motive on Chiaki Suou (the deceased's sister, explicitly flagged in dialogue as having 'the strongest motive'). No culprit discrepancy found -- Karube's own confession in 0633 matches the old file.

clues.desc: Four witness impressions of the fleeing 'culprit' -- large build, plump/springy resistance, unusually nimble, rustling cloth like a dress -- each match the physical behavior of a swinging, opening umbrella rather than a person, once compared side by side.

Karube could not leave with the other guests despite the rain restarting, because his only umbrella (the murder weapon) was gone and his packed spare had been removed by his wife beforehand -- leaving with no umbrella would have exposed the trick.

The mansion's clocks chimed several seconds late after the candles were blown out even though all three on-duty technicians swore their clocks rang exactly on time -- the discrepancy is explained by the great clock's hour hand having been secretly set a few seconds ahead.
